title: Drug reference
description: Static, hand-authored generic medication reference. Like disease_context.schema.json, it does not constrain an LLM response — it validates a curated file matched against a visit's medications by name and fed into the check-in and brief stages as grounding for recognising side effects and monitoring needs. It never contains dosing advice or a recommendation to change a medication.

id.description: Stable slug used as the row's key, e.g. "levothyroxine".

plain_name.description: What a patient would call it, if different from name.

typical_use.description: What it's generally prescribed for, for context only.

aliases.description: Other names a doctor or patient might use for it in a transcript — a doctor often says "synthetic thyroid", never "levothyroxine".

interactions.description: Generic interaction notes, for context only — never a instruction to change anything.

side_effects.description: Known side effects in plain language, used to recognise when a patient's own words describe one — never to suggest stopping or changing the dose.

monitoring_note.description: What's typically monitored while on this drug (e.g. blood tests), for context only.

framing_rule.description: How this file's contents may be surfaced to a patient — e.g. as recognition, never as advice.
